reviewer: Independent director B; separate from generator
scope: All four exact extracted826x460 native endpoint PNGs plus four unscaled native hand/stick detail crops visually inspected. Atlas hash verified against extraction record; no generated video/provider call by reviewer.

takes.intended_action: Short 3.5-second chorus take: controlled alternating rack-tom/snare stroke phases, restrained pulse and downward attention.

source_review.gate: Eligible for bounded motion testing only; no animation, physical-impact, exact-song-sync or whole-cut pass
findings: Same adult drummer identity: long loose wavy dark hair, small pointed chin goatee rather than full beard, silver hoop earrings, black paisley shirt and fitted black jacket with two rows of round brass buttons and ornate sleeve embroidery. No cross or new pendant.

Exactly two separate wooden sticks are visible in each endpoint, one owned by each anatomically connected hand. Grips and wrists are plausible at the native source resolution; no third/spare stick or extra limb is visible.

Stable black five-piece layout: partly cropped front bass drum, two rack toms, floor tom on his RIGHT/viewer-left, snare on his LEFT/viewer-right. Two high cymbals and one lower hi-hat position retain their stand/kit relationship. Closed hi-hat blades should not be confused with an added fourth cymbal position.

Chrome rims/lugs, drums and stands remain broadly fixed within each pair; seated hips and legs are compatible with supported playing. Throne/pedal details are mostly occluded or cropped, so they are not independently certified.
Blue curtains and teal/amber stage light are coherent within each pair. No religious symbol, other band ghost or unattended replacement instrument is visible.

Anatomical RIGHT/viewer-left stick moves from raised over the rack-tom zone to low toward the viewer-left rack-tom rim/head boundary. Its final tip is near the upper rim, not unambiguous proof of a central head strike. Anatomical LEFT/viewer-right stick changes from low near the snare to a modest lifted rebound/next-stroke position. Both changes are reachable without a handoff or large body relocation.
Head makes only a small downward pulse; both forearms remain connected. The static pair is compatible with alternating strokes, not evidence of the intervening pattern.
motion_conditions: Preserve two sticks throughout, one per hand. Stick shafts/tips must remain straight and continuous through grip, approach, impact and rebound; no duplication, vanishing, midair detachment or fused wrist.

Actual percussion must be played: reachable wrist/forearm strokes with controlled elbow and shoulder motion. Head/hair/breath motion or a camera push alone is not an acceptable performance substitute.

Verify physical tip-to-head/cymbal contact densely through generated motion and at natural playback speed. No stick passing through rim/body, hitting empty air while the image asserts an impact, floating cymbal, autonomous wobble, snapping hand or unexplained direction reversal.

Allow only impact-caused small cymbal flex/wobble and stick rebound. Preserve kit/drum/cymbal counts, mount locations, face, costume, hair and seated support; no drum shells breathing, telescoping stands or sliding floor geometry.

No invented exact note/drum synchronization claim from the still sources. Final inserted material needs review against the actual song excerpt and visible causal attacks; pedals are outside this static evidence.

Do not force an apparent through-rim strike merely to hit the endpoint. Stage a causal low rack-tom/head-or-rim approach and rebound, with the left snare stroke/rebound alternating naturally. If generated contact misses or penetrates the rim/head, reject or repair rather than labeling it an exact hit.
Use the short take for an actual controlled 3.5-second chorus pattern; no frozen close or random high-frequency wrist flutter.
limits: Only exact static endpoint plausibility reviewed; no generated video or actual percussion contacts inspected.
Fine finger overlaps, exact bead/head contact and pedal use are limited or unobservable in these826x460 endpoints. Do not claim precise playing accuracy from source acceptance.
